例文
Dear classmates,
Today, I’d like to talk about an important topic: “Smartphone, Tool or Toy?”
Recently, our class conducted a survey on the use of smartphones. Here is the result. 28 students use
smartphones to play games and 10 students use smartphones to watch short videos. Only 12 students use
smartphones to search for information and study.
Using smartphones has both advantages and disadvantages. On the positive side, smartphones can be
very helpful for learning. They provide easy access to a vast amount of information and educational
resources. However, there are also some drawbacks. Excessive use of smartphones can waste a lot of time
and money. Moreover, it can lead to addiction and distract students from their studies.
In my opinion, students should use smartphones wisely. They should set a time limit for
non-educational activities and focus more on using smartphones as a tool for learning.
Thanks a lot for your listening!

My Effective Learning Methods
Our school carried out a survey among 1,200 students on the topic of “My Effective Learning
Methods”. Here are the results.
68% of the students find making study plans the most helpful while 45% think learning by doing
group work seems to be the most effective. 36% believe managing time wisely is useful.
As for me, I prefer to learn by working with a group. I used to be a shy person. As a result, I was
afraid to speak in front of my classmates and I made few friends. Things changed since I began to learn
by working with a group. I joined an English group and made many friends there. We always encouraged
and helped each other. With their support, I became outgoing and confident.
As the saying goes, two heads are better than one. Learning by working with a group works well not
only in improving my English but also in making me more confident.
